questions.question: In a FIFO single-server queue the waiting times follow the Lindley recursion. Why can rejecting a few arriving jobs shorten the waiting times of many later jobs, not just the next one?
options: Each rejection lowers only the next job's wait, by exactly the rejected service time.
The rejected service time is missing from the work carried forward to all later jobs.
A rejection empties the queue, so the next job always starts its service immediately.
Rejected jobs make the server work faster, so later service times become shorter.

questions.question: Under complete acceptance, the candidate waits follow $W_k=[W_{k-1}+I_{k-1}s_{k-1}-x_k]^+$, where $I_{k-1}\in\{0,1\}$ records whether job $k-1$ was accepted. What does the factor $I_{k-1}$ do when job $k-1$ is rejected?
options: It sets $s_{k-1}=0$ in the input list, so the stored service time is overwritten.
It forces $I_k=0$ as well, so that job $k$ is rejected together with job $k-1$.
It drops job $k-1$'s work from job $k$'s wait while the input list stays unchanged.
It resets $W_k$ to $0$, because a rejected job leaves an empty system behind it.

questions.question: In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T>0$ is the threshold. Which acceptance indicator defines the complete rejection rule?
options: $I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k+s_k\leq T\}$
$I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k\leq T\}$
$I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_{k-1}+s_{k-1}\leq T\}$
$I_k=\mathbf{1}\{s_k\leq T\}$

questions.question: In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T\geq0$ is the threshold. Under complete acceptance, $I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k\leq T\}$. If the threshold is lowered to the boundary value $T=0$, which jobs are accepted?
options: No job at all, because a job needs a strictly positive margin below the threshold.
Exactly the jobs whose service time $s_k$ is no larger than their inter-arrival time $x_k$.
Only the first job, since every later job finds at least some work in the system.
Exactly the jobs that arrive when the system holds no work, so that $W_k=0$.

questions.question: In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T>0$ is the threshold. Under partial acceptance, job $k$ receives service $B_k=\min\{T-W_k,s_k\}$. Which guarantee does this rule give?
options: Every job is served completely, and every job waits at most $T$ before it starts.
Every job has sojourn time $W_k+B_k\leq T$, but some jobs are served only in part.
Jobs with $s_k>T$ are rejected, and every other job has sojourn time at most $T$.
Every job waits at most $T$, but its sojourn time can still reach $T+s_k$.

questions.question: In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T>0$ is the threshold. Under complete acceptance with $T=3$, job $k-1$ had $W_{k-1}=4$, was rejected ($I_{k-1}=0$) and has $s_{k-1}=2$; then $x_k=1.5$. What are $W_k$ and the decision for job $k$?
options: $W_k=2.5$; job $k$ is accepted.
$W_k=4.5$; job $k$ is rejected.
$W_k=2.5$; job $k$ is rejected.
$W_k=0$; job $k$ is accepted.

questions.question: Under complete rejection with threshold $T=2$, the first job arrives at an empty FIFO single-server queue with service time $s_1=3$. What are its candidate sojourn time $J_1$ and indicator $I_1$?

In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T>0$ is the threshold. Under partial acceptance with $T=2$, job $k$ finds $W_k=1.5$ and has $s_k=3$. With $B_k=\min\{T-W_k,s_k\}$, what are the accepted service $B_k$ and the sojourn time $J_k$?

Under complete acceptance with $T=2$, five jobs have candidate waits $W=(0,1,3,2,4)$ and indicators $I=(1,1,0,1,0)$. What is the mean waiting time of accepted jobs, $\overline{W}_{\mathrm{accepted}}=\sum_k I_kW_k/\sum_k I_k$?

Under complete acceptance with threshold $T=2$, a job finds candidate wait $W_k=2$ in a FIFO single-server queue and has service time $s_k=3$. What are its sojourn time $J_k=W_k+s_k$ and the decision?
options: $J_k=5$; rejected, since its stay exceeds $T$
$J_k=2$; accepted, its stay capped at $T$
$J_k=5$; accepted, since only $W_k$ is tested
$J_k=3$; accepted, as its queue time is free

questions.question: On the same simulated sample path with threshold $T$, complete rejection (accept iff $W_k+s_k\leq T$) accepted $97\%$ of jobs and complete acceptance (accept iff $W_k\leq T$) only $90\%$. Why can the stricter test accept more jobs?
options: Its test $W_k+s_k\leq T$ is looser, since sojourn times are shorter than waiting times.
Its recursion leaves out the factor $I_{k-1}$, so rejected jobs free more room.
It accepts every job with $s_k\leq T$, and long jobs are rare on such a path.
It turns long jobs away before their work enters, so later jobs find less work.

questions.question: A report claims that complete acceptance cuts the mean wait from $9.20$ to $1.83$, where $9.20$ averages over all jobs with no control and $1.83=\sum_kI_kW_k/\sum_kI_k$ averages over accepted jobs only. What is wrong with this comparison?
options: The two averages cover different sets of jobs; the second drops the largest candidate waits.
Nothing is wrong, because rejected jobs have zero waiting time and can be left out of both averages.
The second average divides by the number of all jobs $n$ instead of the number of accepted jobs.
The controlled path uses shortened service times, so its waits cannot be compared with the original.

questions.question: On one input list $(x_k,s_k)$, let $W_k^{\mathrm{none}}$ be the uncontrolled Lindley waits and $W_k^{\mathrm{CA}}$ the candidate waits under complete acceptance with threshold $T$. Which relation holds for every job $k$?
options: $W_k^{\mathrm{CA}}\leq T$, for rejected jobs as well as for accepted ones
$W_k^{\mathrm{CA}}\leq W_k^{\mathrm{none}}$, for rejected and accepted jobs
$W_k^{\mathrm{CA}}=\min\{W_k^{\mathrm{none}},T\}$, as excess wait is cut off
$W_k^{\mathrm{CA}}\leq W_k^{\mathrm{none}}$ for accepted jobs, but it can fail for rejected ones

questions.question: Under complete acceptance with $T=2$, a FIFO single-server queue starts empty; five jobs have service times $s=(1,4,3,2,1)$ and inter-arrival times $x_k=2$ for $k\geq2$. Using $W_k=[W_{k-1}+I_{k-1}s_{k-1}-x_k]^+$ and $I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k\leq T\}$, which jobs are accepted?

Under complete rejection with $T=3$, a FIFO single-server queue starts empty; five jobs have $s=(1,3,2,1,2)$ and $x_k=1$ for $k\geq2$. Waits follow $W_k=[W_{k-1}+I_{k-1}s_{k-1}-x_k]^+$ and $I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k+s_k\leq T\}$. What is the fraction $a=\frac{1}{n}\sum_kI_k$ of accepted jobs?

Under partial acceptance with $T=2$, a FIFO single-server queue starts empty; four jobs have $s=(3,1,4,1)$ and $x_k=1$ for $k\geq2$. With $B_1=\min\{T,s_1\}$, $W_k=[W_{k-1}+B_{k-1}-x_k]^+$ and $B_k=\min\{T-W_k,s_k\}$, what is the total accepted work $\sum_kB_k$?

In a FIFO single-server queue that starts empty, job $k$ has inter-arrival time $x_k$ and service time $s_k$; $I_k=1$ if job $k$ is accepted, $W_k$ is its candidate waiting time and $T>0$ is the threshold. Under complete rejection, job $k$ is accepted iff $W_k+s_k\leq T$. Which statement correctly relates the condition $s_k\leq T$ to the acceptance of job $k$?
options: Every job with $s_k\leq T$ is accepted, while an accepted job may have $s_k>T$.
A job is accepted exactly when $s_k\leq T$, whatever wait $W_k$ it finds.
Every accepted job has $s_k\leq T$, but a job with $s_k\leq T$ can be rejected.
An accepted job may have $s_k>T$, and a job with $s_k\leq T$ may be rejected.

questions.question: Partial acceptance with threshold $T$ sets $B_1=\min\{T,s_1\}$, $W_k=[W_{k-1}+B_{k-1}-x_k]^+$ and $B_k=\min\{T-W_k,s_k\}$, with $J_k=W_k+B_k$. Why is $B_k\geq0$ for every job, so that it is a valid accepted amount?
options: Because $s_k\geq0$, and the minimum of two numbers inherits the sign of either one.
Because jobs whose wait exceeds $T$ are rejected before $B_k$ is computed.
Because the inter-arrival time $x_k$ is always at least $T$ under partial acceptance.
Because $W_k=[J_{k-1}-x_k]^+\leq J_{k-1}\leq T$, so $T-W_k$ is never negative.

questions.question: Jobs arrive at rate $\lambda=1$ with mean service time $1/1.1\approx0.91$ at one server. Complete rejection accepts a fraction $0.97$ of arrivals, and the accepted jobs have mean service time $0.75$. Assuming accepted jobs depart at the rate they are admitted, what is the server utilization (long-run fraction of time busy)?
options: about $0.91$
about $0.73$
about $0.88$
about $0.97$

questions.question: Under complete acceptance, a FIFO single-server queue starts empty; four jobs have $s=(3,3,1,1)$ and $x_k=1$ for $k\geq2$, with $W_k=[W_{k-1}+I_{k-1}s_{k-1}-x_k]^+$ and $I_k=\mathbf{1}\{W_k\leq T\}$. How many jobs are accepted with $T=1$ and with $T=2$, respectively?
options: $3$ with $T=1$; $2$ with $T=2$
$2$ with $T=1$; $3$ with $T=2$
$1$ with $T=1$; $2$ with $T=2$
$3$ with $T=1$; $4$ with $T=2$
